newsitem.title: ITALY: Trial sought for Italy's Prime Minister Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Trial sought for Italy's Prime Minister Prodi.

text.p: An Italian magistrate recommended on Monday that Prime Minister Romano Prodi should be tried for alleged abuse of office during his chairmanship of giant state industrial holding IRI.
Prodi, who has led a centre-left government since May, reacted calmly to the news, telling journalists that he had done no wrong and had full confidence in Italy's judicial system.

"The indictment request certainly does not put my personal honesty at stake," Prodi told a news conference in the northeast town of Udine, where he was on a visit. "It doesn't worry me and it doesn't put me in difficulty," he said.

The requested indictment, lodged with court officials in Rome by deputy public prosecutor Giuseppa Geremia, relates to alleged irregularities in the sale by IRI in October 1993 of food unit Cirio to a southern consortium, Fis.Vi.

The ANSA and AGI news agencies said Geremia had asked that Prodi and the five other members of the IRI board at the time, including senior Treasury official Mario Draghi, should be charged with complicity in abuse of office.
Fis.Vi's director Carlo Saverio Lamiranda faced similar charges, the reports said.

The recommendation must be reviewed by an examining judge, Edoardo Landi, who will decide whether formal charges and a trial should follow. The offence carries a prison sentence of two to five years in the event of a conviction.
Landi can also decide to drop the case or order further investigations. It was not immediately clear when the hearing would take place.

News of the move struck like a bombshell on the day the Italian lira returned to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) after a four-year absence in a step hailed by Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi as a sign of new-found stability.

Stocks, bonds and the lira, sensitive to the judicial storms that have battered Italian politics since the country's corruption scandals broke in 1992, all lost ground on reports of the indictment request.
The lira, which returned to the ERM at a central rate of 990 to the German mark, slipped to 993 before recovering ground.

Prodi, a respected economist who entered politics only in 1995, was chairman of IRI, the debt-laden holding company that groups Italy's state industries, for most of the 1980s and again for a year from May 1993.

Geremia's investigation into the Cirio sale, part of a privatisation drive initiated by Prodi, began in February after a complaint from a small shareholder and questions in parliament from the opposition hard-right National Alliance party.

The news agency reports said her enquiry had concluded that Fis.Vi, a consortium of southern Italian cooperatives, banks and businessmen, had gained an "unjust advantage" in the purchase as a result of actions by IRI's board.
Previously published reports say the investigation focused on interest rates, guarantees and other details of the sale.
Fis.Vi bought 62 percent of Cirio for 310 billion lire ($206 million) but no longer owns the food company.
Geremia questioned Prodi last March, one month before his centre-left coalition's general election victory, when he testified that the sale had been in order.
"I have always acted openly and extremely correctly," Prodi said on Monday.
